title: Warranty failures of two pump seal designs
intro:
A pump maker tracked two shaft-seal designs in the field for one year. Of 400 pumps with seal A, 22 failed within the warranty year; of 420 pumps with seal B, 45 did. Do the failure rates differ? With p₁ for seal A and p₂ for seal B, test H₀: p₁ = p₂ against H₁: p₁ ≠ p₂ at α = 0.05 with the **two-proportion z-test** (pooled), and find the 95 % confidence interval for p₁ − p₂.

Find z, the two-sided p-value, and the two ends of the interval. Give z to two decimals, p to four decimals or more (it is small), and the interval to three decimals or more.

To use the Workbench: press Ctrl+B and choose **Two-sample test**. Set **Test** to *Two proportions (pooled z)*, **Data from** to *Summary statistics entered here*, **Alternative hypothesis** to *Two-sided (≠)* and **Significance level (α)** to 0.05, then type **Successes in sample 1 (x₁)** = 22, **Sample 1 size (n₁)** = 400, **Successes in sample 2 (x₂)** = 45 and **Sample 2 size (n₂)** = 420. A "success" is just the outcome counted, here a failed seal. Ctrl+L brings you back.

ask.prompt: 95 % CI for p₁ − p₂, lower end
95 % CI for p₁ − p₂, upper end

Statistic.says: That z uses the unpooled standard error, √(p̂₁(1 − p̂₁)/n₁ + p̂₂(1 − p̂₂)/n₂). The test assumes H₀: p₁ = p₂, so it uses one pooled p̂ = (x₁ + x₂)/(n₁ + n₂) in the standard error.
Check the sign. z = (p̂₁ − p̂₂)/SE with seal A first, and seal A has the lower failure rate, so z is negative.

PValue.says: That is a one-tailed p-value. H₁ is two-sided (≠), so p = 2 × P(Z > |z|).
That p-value comes from the unpooled z. The test uses the pooled standard error.

CiLower.says: Check the order: the interval is for p₁ − p₂, seal A minus seal B, and seal A fails less often, so both ends are negative.

CiUpper.says: Check the order: the interval is for p₁ − p₂, seal A minus seal B, and seal A fails less often, so both ends are negative.

hints: The sample proportions are p̂₁ = 22/400 and p̂₂ = 45/420. The pooled proportion is p̂ = (22 + 45)/(400 + 420).
Test: z = (p̂₁ − p̂₂)/√(p̂(1 − p̂)(1/n₁ + 1/n₂)) with the pooled p̂, and p = 2 × P(Z > |z|): Python 2 * stats.norm.sf(abs(z)), R 2 * pnorm(abs(z), lower.tail = FALSE).
Interval: (p̂₁ − p̂₂) ± 1.96 × √(p̂₁(1 − p̂₁)/n₁ + p̂₂(1 − p̂₂)/n₂), with each sample's own proportion, not the pooled one.
